title: Pebble Keep
logline: Merge stone golems on a tiny garden board to stop a comedic snail horde from reaching the keep gate, in one-thumb runs of about three minutes.
player_fantasy: You are the young keeper of a crumbling garden keep, waking stone golems and fusing them into mighty guardians.
hook: Every win restores a piece of a cosy keep you can see, and the restored keep wakes new golem families: the meta feeds the core instead of sitting beside it.
pillars: Every merge is a visible power spike

comparables.title: Rush Royale
comparables.change: solo PvE, deterministic family merges, portrait one-thumb

comparables.title: Royal Match
comparables.change: renovation unlocks gameplay (golem families), not only decoration

risks: Crowded merge-defense space; the creative must sell the keep and the snails, not the merge

risks.mitigation: shuffled spawn bag, bot-tested worst cases

kill_criteria: Greybox prototype: fewer than 6 of 10 persona playtests choose a second run unprompted after two iterations
Creative test: no creative of 5 reaches the CPI ceiling set before the test
rationale: Strongest agent-buildability of the five shortlisted concepts: a deterministic grid sim, 2D assets with a narrow style, data-driven levels and solver-verifiable bonus puzzles. Weighted total uses fun_potential x2, market x1.5 and the rest x1 (63.5 / 8.5 = 7.47). Novelty is its weakest score; the keep-unlocks-families hook and the snail humour are the differentiation bets the creative test must validate.
